exclusion_detail: The abstract names a set of fifteen potent conjugates (13b-e, 13h-j, 14c-d, 15a, 15c-d, 16b, 16d, 18f) and a follow-up set of five (13b, 13c, 13d, 16b, 14d); the text calls 13c, 13d, 16b and 14d the 'most active' and runs the same mechanism and docking experiments on all of them. No single lead is named.

lead.label: none (13b/13c/13d/14d/16b as a set)
lead.why: Abstract: 'Conjugates 13b, 13c, 13d, 16b and 14d were also evaluated ... The promising candidates induced cell cycle arrest ...'

notes: Every conjugate is made by Claisen-Schmidt condensation of a pyrazole-5-carbaldehyde (12a-d), which itself needs four steps from an acetophenone (oxalate condensation, pyrazole formation, LiAlH4 reduction, IBX oxidation), so every compound is 5 steps, over the limit even if a lead were chosen.
